attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He states them in his own voice; they are not quoted from the Axios report or the Super PAC statement.

semantics.note: This is a retrospective description of how Trump's AI stance had changed by the post date. The 'not entirely bolted yet' qualifier is kept. The 'yet' hints at further change but adds no scored forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary. Official presidential action, an EO plus White House rollout meetings, counts as 'strongly encouraging', and 'full anti AI regulation' means the earlier hands-off, deregulatory stance. The result depends on how much weight 'strongly' carries.

evidence.note: Primary text of the June 2 EO. It directs agencies to design a voluntary framework giving the government pre-release access to covered frontier models for up to 30 days.
Independent NPR report from June 2 calling the order a shift from the administration's hands-off approach. This supports 'changed course'.
CNBC, Aug 3: the White House was hosting leading labs to roll out the completed voluntary framework. This is active promotion before the Aug 20 post.
Trump scrapped a stronger draft in May, and the final order is narrower, cyber-focused and voluntary. This tempers 'strongly' but does not undo the shift.

reviews.rationale: Before Aug 20, 2026, Trump signed an EO setting up a voluntary 30-day pre-release access framework for frontier models (e1). NPR called it a shift from the hands-off approach (e2). The White House then met with labs to promote the finished framework (e3). The narrowed scope and the scrapped stronger draft (e4) temper 'strongly' but do not contradict the shift. The support condition is met under a fair plain reading.
